answer: A work-history kernel defends an agent economy: each identity earns non-transferable reputation only by completing verified tasks over time, and rewards follow that history, not raw account count. A newcomer may wander in, but without successful work its claims carry little weight. An attacker flooding the system must pay the full time and task cost for every fake identity, while honest agents ride the tide of prior performance. Thousands of shells buy no influence, because influence is earned slowly and cannot be copied or transferred.
